verdict.rationale: Svelte has no built-in natural-language command interface of its own. It does ship a first-party MCP server (docs lookup plus the svelte-autofixer static analysis) and subagents, which let a user drive Svelte development by giving natural-language instructions to an AI agent. The natural-language layer itself comes from the host agent, not from Svelte. missing for 10: a native natural-language command interface in the product, evidence that the agent tooling covers operating the CLI and project lifecycle by natural language, independent or hands-on corroboration of the MCP workflow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: The Svelte MCP (Model Context Protocol) server can help your agent write better Svelte code. It works by providing relevant documentation, and statically analysing generated code
claude mcp add -t stdio -s [scope] svelte -- npx -y @sveltejs/mcp
svelte-autofixer: Analyzes Svelte code and returns issues and suggestions.
Subagents: focused agents that can be invoked in parallel to execute atomic operations in a separate context window
